identity.title: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Language for Interpretability

problem.claim: Interpret model representations and computations as human-understandable concepts.

gap.claim: Existing Sparse Autoencoders often recover token-specific, noisy, or highly local concepts, partly because they neglect language's temporal structure.

contributions.claim: Introduces Temporal Sparse Autoencoders with a contrastive loss that encourages high-level feature activations to remain consistent across adjacent tokens.
Reports that the modification separates semantic and syntactic features in a self-supervised setting and recovers smoother, more coherent semantic concepts.

stated_novelty.claim: A contrastive temporal-consistency modification to SAEs for unsupervised language-model interpretability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report smoother and more coherent semantic concepts across multiple datasets and models, without sacrificing reconstruction quality.
The authors report clear semantic structure despite training without explicit semantic supervision.

narrative_sequence.summary: Interpretability seeks human-understandable concepts from model representations and computations.
Recent SAEs often produce token-specific, noisy, or local concepts.
The abstract attributes this limitation to neglected temporal structure and proposes T-SAEs with adjacent-token contrastive consistency.
The authors report semantic–syntactic disentanglement, smoother concepts, preserved reconstruction quality, and emergent semantic structure without explicit semantic signals.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a concrete failure mode—local, noisy features—to a structural property of language and then modifies the objective to reflect that property.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research framing connects an observed representation failure to an omitted data structure, making the proposed intervention diagnostically motivated.
lessons.application: When presenting a representation-learning method, identify the specific structure omitted by the baseline and encode it directly in the training objective.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target phenomenon is intentionally local or when enforcing cross-position consistency could erase meaningful changes.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, baselines, dataset/model identities, or definition of the reconstruction-quality comparison.
The extent and evaluation of semantic–syntactic disentanglement are unspecified.
